card.name: Past-tense verbs in narrative web prose
card.fires_on: Small verbs and helpers such as was, had, didn't, remained, and to, right after a subject in general web prose, mostly history or reports. The next word is likely a past-tense description.

modes.label: Past-tense be/have after a subject
modes.description: The verb was, had, or remained follows a noun subject in a descriptive past-tense statement.
modes.example: The government's human rights record<< remained>> poor.

modes.label: Helper or particle in a clause
modes.description: A small word such as to, a, or 's sits mid-clause before a completion.
modes.example: Atticus always said, "to understand someone, you had<< to>> ____."

card.writes: It suppresses time-reference words like originally, previously, recently, and their Chinese and Russian equivalents, so it discourages adding a time adverb here.
card.plain: It fires on small verbs in past-tense descriptions and makes the model less likely to insert words like 'previously' or 'originally' next.
